summary: In this excerpt from Book 10 (part 25) of a novel, Lawrence, a former member of the Order, confronts Randy, a man who has just revealed himself as Securitat, after a restaurant dinner. Randy says he has evaluated Lawrence's work and dismisses his performance as a private eye, noting he would have been harassing Anja's neighbors without intervention. Lawrence angrily accuses the world of treating honest people like criminals, pushing them to act that way, while Randy argues the reverse causal direction. The scene ends with Lawrence slamming the table and Randy rising as bulky figures emerge from the shadows.
one_line: Lawrence, a former Order member, clashes with Randy, a Securitat agent, over criminality and treatment after a tense restaurant dinner.
key_facts: Randy tells Lawrence he is 88th percentile in intelligence and could likely score higher based on evaluated work.
Lawrence had not been much of a cash user before he went into the Order and had seen hardly any cash spent since returning to the world.
Randy says Lawrence's performance as a private eye is not very good.
Randy claims that without his intervention, Lawrence would still be standing outside Anja's apartment building harassing her neighbors.
Lawrence says Randy is Securitat, and Randy replies, "Let me put it this way... I'm not one of Anja's neighbors."
Randy tells Lawrence that he lied to the Securitat man at Penn Station that day.
Lawrence claims that from the minute he stepped out of the Order, everyone treated him like a criminal, which made him act like one.
Lawrence argues that the causal arrow runs the other direction: the world treats people like crooks, so the only way to get by is to act criminal.
Randy asks whether the Order builds a wall to keep outsiders out because they are barbarians and to keep members in because they are too fragile.
Lawrence slaps his hand on the table, making the crystal ring, and Randy stands as bulky figures step out of the shadows behind them.
Lawrence describes Sara as lovely and says she and he once had a thing together.
Lawrence's pan, a device that gives him feedback, warns him he is getting edgy, and he shushes it.
